headline: High risk of shared-project write conflicts and prompt/data leakage via gpt-engineer’s project directory; plano’s gateway role adds downstream propagation risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-engineer reads and writes the user project directory and has no self-isolation by default; plano can ingest config and route chat completions. If plano forwards gpt-engineer outputs or shared files without provenance checks, injected instructions in project files can influence downstream behavior. The pairwise bridge is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same project directory
IF plano consumes file-derived content or model outputs without provenance filtering
mitigations: Separate the project directory from any plano-managed workspace
Add a manual review step before plano consumes generated files
Prefix untrusted file content with explicit non-instruction markers
Disable automatic ingestion of project files into prompts
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between file reads and prompt assembly

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-engineer can read the filesystem, execute shell, and has broad network egress; plano sends data to an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint and touches logs/metrics. If both see the same workspace, generated code or secrets can flow from A into B’s outbound requests or telemetry. The leakage path is credible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF the same workspace contains secrets or sensitive source code
IF plano forwards file contents, traces, or logs to its backend
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared project directory
Redact sensitive files before either agent runs
Restrict plano logging to metadata only
Use separate credentials and workspaces for each agent
requires-engineering: enforce content filtering before API calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: gpt-engineer has write_filesystem and per-project shared state via the project directory; plano also reads/writes config.yaml and supports no multiple instances. Concurrent access to the same mutable workspace can overwrite files or config without locking. This is a default-dangerous overlap because neither profile shows coordination primitives.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same project directory
IF either agent writes while the other is reading or editing config/state
mitigations: Run the agents in separate directories
Serialize access with a simple manual lock file
Back up the workspace before each run
Avoid concurrent edits to config.yaml
requires-engineering: add OS-level file locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-engineer produces generated code and plano is an AI gateway that can route model calls; if plano treats A’s outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream prompts or actions. The profiles do not show verification or critique by default, so the safer assumption is that A’s output may be reused by B.
conditions: IF plano uses gpt-engineer output as prompt material or routing input
IF no human or automated verification step checks the generated code or facts
mitigations: Insert a review step before B consumes A’s output
Require citations or diffs for any reused content
Limit B to summarizing rather than acting on A’s output
Log provenance for each handoff
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, but gpt-engineer explicitly handles OPENAI_API_KEY and broad network egress while plano sends data to an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and records logs/metrics. This creates a modest compliance mismatch risk around retention and secret handling, though no specific residency or regulated-data violation is stated.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in the shared project directory
IF plano logs request contents or traces containing sensitive material
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair’s workspace
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately
Disable verbose logging in plano
Review retention settings before deployment
requires-engineering: add data-class-based retention controls
